items.title: Constable Muhammad Raimi laid to rest after electric shock tragedy
items.summary: DUNGUN: Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee who was believed to have died from an electric shock in Kampung Weston, Beaufort, Sabah yesterday, was laid to rest at the Felda Kerteh 2 Muslim Cemetery here at 1.15 am today. The vehicle carrying the late Muhammad Raimi, 24, arrived at his residence in Felda Kerteh 2 at 11.40pm for the final respects and funeral prayers before the burial. The funeral prayers for the late Muhammad Raimi were led by Terengganu State Education, Higher Education, Science, Technology and Human Development Committee chairman Datuk Satiful Bahari Mamat.

items.title: US Senate passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Senate on Friday passed a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia's energy revenues. "This could finally bring Russia to the negotiating table and end this conflict" between Russia and Ukraine, said Republican Jim Risch, chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. New sanctions against Russian President Vladimir Putin and other high-ranking officials are also to be imposed.

items.title: Beyond fines: Demanding real accountability for social security exploitation
items.summary: LETTERS: The news that at least 100 people face fraud charges over bogus claims under Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 programme is deeply troubling. Those who exploit social security systems treat workers' hard-earned contributions as easy pickings, and such behaviour must never be excused or downplayed. Perkeso must now put far stronger safeguards in place.

items.title: Selangor targets RM600b economy
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor aims to grow its economy to RM600 billion by 2030 under its second five-year development plan, which seeks to strengthen the state's position as Malaysia's economic powerhouse while creating more high-paying jobs for its people. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state, which contributes 26.5 per cent to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP), would pursue a more ambitious growth strategy under the Second Selangor Plan (RS2) 2026-2030. "We are confident that during the Second Selangor Plan, the value of Selangor's economy can reach RM600 billion," he said when tabling the RS2 motion at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly yesterday.

items.title: PKR urged to confront hard truths after election setbacks [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR must use its coming national congress for reflection in the wake of successive electoral defeats, an exodus from its ranks and its deputy president's taking leave. Treasurer-general William Leong said the party, led by president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, must provide clarity over the issues that have plagued PKR since it came to power in Putrajaya and its plans to turn things around. Leong said PKR grassroots must remain steadfast and united.

items.title: Stay or go? DAP faces catch-22 as crucial congress vote looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — DAP delegates will gather on August 16 for the party’s national congress, where they will face a political catch-22 that could shape its strategy heading into the next general election. Roughly 4,000 delegates are expected to vote on whether DAP leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Parliament. Many voters may not distinguish between leaving the executive and continuing to support the government in Parliament.

items.title: US appeals court orders halt to Trump ballroom construction
items.summary: WASHINGTON: An appeals court dealt a blow to US President Donald Trump's prized White House ballroom project on Friday, upholding a judge's ruling that construction must halt since Congress had not approved it. The appeals court, which had temporarily allowed construction to continue while it considered the case, upheld the lower court's ruling but stayed its own decision for two weeks, giving Trump time to ask the Supreme Court to intervene. A three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit ruled 2-1 to uphold the district court order to halt construction above ground, while allowing work to continue below ground, where a military bunker is planned.

items.title: NST Leader: Stopping the theft of public funds
items.summary: The government — through its agencies and statutory bodies — has come up with many programmes to bring some measure of relief to people hard done by circumstances. These initiatives involve large sums from the public purse — i.e. Ask most people on the street who is the likely culprit siphoning public funds and the answer is more often than not "a government officer".

items.title: US unexpectedly loses jobs in setback for Trump ahead of midterms
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States unexpectedly lost thousands of jobs in July, government data showed Friday, a blow to US President Donald Trump's claims of leading an economic revival as his Republican party gears up for crucial midterm elections. The world's largest economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, data published by the US Bureau of Labour Statistics showed, signalling potential labour market weakness after months of steady growth. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 per cent, likely a result of falling labour supply as the US economy grapples with an aging population and lower net migration.

items.title: Elderly man killed when BMW crashes into driving institute fence
items.summary: MARANG: An elderly man was killed when the BMW he was driving skidded and crashed into the fence of a driving institute along Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kuantan, near Alur Tuman, here on Friday. District police chief Superintendent Mohd Sofian Redzuan said they received a call from the public regarding the accident in front of the driving institute at 7.30am. He said initial investigations found that the 65-year-old victim was driving from Masjid Kelulut to his home in Pulau Kerengga when he lost control of the vehicle, causing it to veer onto the right shoulder of the road before crashing into the fence of the driving institute.

items.title: Hamzah says party decisions do not represent PN position
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: The views or decisions of an individual political party should not be regarded as representing Perikatan Nasional (PN), as the coalition is governed by its own constitution and decision-making mechanisms, said Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin. Hamzah said PN was a coalition comprising several political parties, each governed by its own constitution and internal procedures. "For Wawasan, however, any amendment to the party constitution must be made through an extraordinary general meeting involving delegates.

items.title: Khairul Aming hits RM2mil in 2 minutes in TikTok sales
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Influencer and entrepreneur Khairul Aming took just two minutes to rack up RM2 million in sales of his latest products on TikTok. Among the new products was Rendang Nyet Berapi, Dendeng Nyet Ekstra Pedas and Oriental Kopi Putih Premium. The sales broke his personal record, reflecting the significant influence content creators have on digital sales.

items.title: Speaker Johari: Wong Chen told me he wanted to resign as MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul says PKR's Wong Chen had voiced his intentions to resign as Subang member of parliament. Instead, the three-term MP only said he would issue a statement on Monday regarding the letter and his meeting with Johari. "This morning, I had a longer than expected meeting with Tan Sri Johari, the Speaker of Dewan Rakyat.

items.title: Widow never expected policeman husband to return home in a coffin
items.summary: SIBU: Corporal Chiu Teck Siong's widow, Tan Wei Wei, 39, never imagined her husband would "return" earlier than his scheduled leave on Aug 27. Tan said Chiu had long wished to be transferred to Sibu so the family could live together. I never expected he would return like this," she said at the Ching Chuan Sibu Mortuary Hall.

items.title: No rift between BN and PN, says Hamzah
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Parti Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has dismissed speculation of strained relations between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN), describing such claims as attempts to sow division. How can people already say there is a rift? Hamzah said he had also heard remarks by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang and maintained that there were no problems between the parties.

items.title: Freelance host, businessman arrested for podcast episode that touched on 3R
items.summary: KLANG: Police confirmed the arrest of two men following a report received regarding a podcast episode that allegedly touched on religious sensitivities. Klang Utara police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received the report on Aug 5 before the arrests of a freelance host and a businessman, aged in their 30s and 60s respectively, were carried out yesterday. "Police have received a report regarding a video clip of a podcast created by two individuals discussing the issues of secular and liberal ideologies.

items.title: Anwar: Party differences should not hinder friendship, cooperation for people's benefit
items.summary: MELAKA: Differences in the political parties governing the federal and state governments should not stand in the way of friendship and cooperation between them, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said close ties and cooperation were essential to ensure the people continued to benefit from government initiatives. "Our system of government requires close cooperation.

items.title: [UPDATED] Hamzah: BN, PN must compromise on Melaka seats to sustain 'Blue Wave'
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional must be prepared to compromise on seat allocations in Melaka if they want to sustain the "Blue Wave" momentum, said Parti Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin. "If we want to keep that wave going, we must have a spirit of compromise," Hamzah told reporters after the party's extraordinary general meeting here today. His remarks came after BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition intended to defend all 21 seats it currently held in the state, potentially leaving just seven of Melaka's 28 seats for its partners.

items.title: Tesla's FSD secrecy raises troubling safety questions
items.summary: FOUR months ago, the Netherlands approved Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system and has since then advocated for its adoption across the European Union. Releasing such details would violate Tesla's commercial secrets, the regulator said, echoing the automaker's own demands on the regulator for confidentiality. Since late 2024, Tesla has pressed RDW to keep documentation about the FSD safety review secret, according to previously unreported email correspondence between the Dutch regulator and Tesla, obtained through a public-records request.

items.title: Anwar announces RM1.29mil allocation for Melaka Islamic schools
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: The government has approved RM1.29 million for 13 maintenance and repair projects at Islamic education institutions (IPI), including Sekolah Agama Rakyat (SAR) under the Melaka Islamic Religious Department (Jaim) this year. He said the government was concerned about the condition of Islamic education institutions, including pondok schools and tahfiz centres nationwide, which had been neglected without funding, while also balancing assistance for Chinese and Indian schools. "Other recipients include Sekolah Agama Rakyat (SAR) Jaim Durian Tunggal with RM140,000, SAR Jaim Tebong, Jasin (RM30,000), SAR Jaim Kampung Baru (RM50,000), SAR Jaim Serkam Darat (RM70,000) and SAR Jaim Taman Maju, Jasin (RM100,000)," he said in his speech.

items.title: The AI boom's emerging market reality
items.summary: A few years ago, when almost every bank research note seemed to focus on soaring United States tech stocks, veteran emerging market fund manager Carlos von Hardenberg was struggling to get investors interested in anything else. Now the artificial intelligence boom has lit a rocket under the South Korean and Taiwanese firms that dominate high-tech memory chip making and, as of this year, the global EM stock indexes that have emerged from Wall Street's shadow. Taiwan's TSMC, by far the biggest company in the EM stock universe, fell almost 14 per cent.

items.title: Rauf: Melaka advances sustainable landscape development
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka has established a strong foundation for sustainable landscape development through the enforcement of the Tree Preservation Order under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976. This, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, safeguards high-value trees that form an integral part of the state's landscape heritage. He said the introduction of the Melaka Landscape Guidelines in 2022 had further strengthened the foundation by providing a comprehensive framework for implementing agencies, local authorities, developers and stakeholders to undertake landscape development in a planned, high-quality, distinctive and sustainable manner.

items.title: Thai students left in disbelief after deadly school shooting
items.summary: NONTHABURI, Thailand: Sobbing Thai students embraced each other tightly on Friday after a 14-year-old classmate entered their school wielding his grandfather's handgun and shot dead at least five school staff. Tearful students in school uniforms held each other outside the Debsirin Nonthaburi secondary school while emergency workers treated injuries and parents looked for their children. We just ran," the 17-year-old said.

items.title: Malaysia, Singapore to strengthen labour cooperation, gig worker protection
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Singapore will continue to strengthen cooperation in the labour sector, including enhancing the welfare and protection of gig workers, as both countries navigate an increasingly dynamic employment landscape. He said both sides exchanged views on current labour market developments and the challenges facing Malaysia and Singapore in preparing their workforce to meet the demands of the future economy. "Malaysia and Singapore are facing rapid changes in the employment landscape.

items.title: 'Efforts to increase defence allocation reflects govt's commitment to modernise armed forces'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's plan to increase the defence allocation under the 2027 Budget reflects the government's commitment to modernising the armed forces. Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the military appreciated the government's commitment to strengthening the forces' development, operational readiness and the welfare of its personnel and their families. Earlier today, Anwar said at the Semarak Kenegaraan programme with the armed forces at Terendak Camp in Melaka that the government would seek to increase the defence allocation under next year's budget.

items.title: Bodies of three policemen killed in electrocution tragedy flown home [WATCH]
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The bodies of three policemen electrocuted to death in Beaufort yesterday were flown to their respective hometowns tonight aboard Royal Malaysian Air Force and police aircraft. Bernama observed the RMAF aircraft carrying the bodies of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee depart from Kota Kinabalu International Airport about 7.10pm. The body of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong was taken to the police air wing base here before being flown to Sarawak aboard a police aircraft.

items.title: Home, Transport ministries given two weeks to submit airport security plan to cabinet
items.summary: SANDAKAN: The cabinet has given the Home and Transport ministries two weeks to submit a comprehensive plan to strengthen airport security. "Immediate steps are being taken to draft a detailed improvement plan involving various agencies," he told reporters after visiting several islands in the Eastern Sabah Security Zone (Ess Zone) with foreign diplomats. Also present were Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos and its chief executive officer Datuk Dr Jamaluddin Mohd Ali.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - August 7, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Hadi's claim disputed Bersatu disputed PAS president's claim its Perikatan Nasional membership lapsed after Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin announced plans to form a new coalition. Ex-DJ sentenced Former radio presenter Ismahalil Hamzah sentenced to 30 years after Court of Appeal overturned his High Court acquittal in drug case. Ex‑PM charges Datuk Ismail Sabri Yaakob set to become third ex‑prime minister facing criminal charges, after Datuk Seri Najib Razak and Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin.

items.title: Bank Negara governor: Malaysia remains resilient in facing global crises
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia successfully weathered various global crises, including the Asian financial crisis, the Covid-19 pandemic and conflicts in the Middle East while maintaining the resilience of the country's economic fundamentals Bank Negara Malaysia Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the achievement was supported by four key buffers, namely economic and trading partner diversification, clear economic policies, sufficient fiscal space, and strong international reserves. He said the experience of facing several previous crises has taught Malaysia not to depend on any particular economic sector or trading partner. Rasheed said clear policies continue to support the country's economic fundamentals despite facing uncertainties, while sufficient fiscal space enables the government to address economic shocks.

items.title: MACC completes 4-day interview in RM370mil share purchase probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today completed a four-day interview with a former chief financial officer of a company owned by a statutory body as part of investigations into alleged abuse of power involving the purchase of shares in two plantation companies worth about RM370 million. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today marked the fourth and final day of questioning the former senior officer, who was first called in on Tuesday. "Today was the final day for the MACC to record the former senior officer's statement," he said.

items.title: Anwar questions RM330m gap in proposed Felda hotel sale, orders full report
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) to provide a complete report regarding the proposed sale of a hotel owned by the agency, which was allegedly at a price far lower than the original purchase price. “Felda is under my watch. “Felda settlers are struggling.

items.title: Anwar: Govt to cut red tape in military, police promotion process
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said details of the new mechanism are expected to be announced during the Ambang Merdeka celebration at Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on August 30. He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz are currently finalising the implementation mechanism. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Mohd Na’im Mokhtar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Shamsul Azri and Army Chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: Malaysia and Singapore to deepen labour cooperation, boost protection for gig workers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia and Singapore will continue to strengthen cooperation in the labour sector, including enhancing the welfare and protection of gig workers, as both countries navigate an increasingly dynamic employment landscape. He said both sides exchanged views on current labour market developments and the challenges facing Malaysia and Singapore in preparing their workforce to meet the demands of the future economy. “Malaysia and Singapore are facing rapid changes in the employment landscape.

items.title: Woman hurt after SUV crashes into KKIA departure hall
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — A woman was injured after the sport utility vehicle (SUV) she was driving reportedly lost control and crashed through the glass entrance of the departure hall at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) this afternoon. The incident, which occurred at about 4.20pm, shattered the glass doors of the departure hall and sent broken glass across the passenger walkway, causing panic among members of the public at the scene. Early indications suggest the driver may have accidentally pressed the accelerator, causing the vehicle to surge forward and crash into the terminal.

items.title: Ismail Sabri stable after successful pacemaker implantation at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob’s pacemaker implantation procedure this afternoon at the National Heart Institute (IJN) was carried out successfully, his lawyer has confirmed. When contacted by Malay Mail , Ismail Sabri’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad confirmed that “the procedure went smoothly and was successful”. IJN later said Ismail Sabri had successfully undergone a leadless pacemaker implantation procedure for an abnormal heart rhythm this afternoon.

items.title: Malaysia to increase defence spending in Budget 2027, says Anwar
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 7 — The government will seek to increase defence allocation in Budget 2027 to strengthen the Malaysian Armed Forces’ (MAF) readiness and improve personnel welfare, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said greater investment was necessary to safeguard national peace, which he described as the country’s most valuable asset. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Army chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.

items.title: MACC urges ministry chiefs to protect whistleblowers as Malaysia eyes higher CPI ranking
items.summary: MACC’s National Governance Planning Division deputy director Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the move is critical to remove civil servants’ fear of reporting misconduct and, in turn, bolster organisational integrity. He said secretaries-general and directors-general must translate the government’s commitment to amending the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010 down to the grassroots level, to ensure that the Integrity Unit in every ministry functions independently and reports directly to the MACC. Mohd Gunawan said that beyond strengthening whistleblower protection, secretaries-general and directors-general must lead comprehensive reforms in public procurement and contract systems, including full open tenders and mandatory declarations of beneficial ownership for all bidding companies.

items.title: Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah launches Women in Technology Awards 2026 to honour Malaysian innovators
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Yayasan Tuanku Fauziah (YTF) has launched the Women in Technology Awards 2026, a national initiative to recognise outstanding Malaysian women, whose leadership, innovation and technological achievements are shaping the country’s future. Two categories will be offered — the Senior Women in Technology Award, worth RM30,000, for professionals with at least 20 years’ experience, and the Junior Women in Technology Award, worth RM15,000, for innovators aged 35 and below or with under 10 years’ experience. YTF said the awards celebrate exceptional Malaysian women whose contributions have advanced science, technology and innovation, inspiring greater participation in STEM and encouraging future generations of innovators and leaders.

items.title: Immigration Dept gears up for F1 Bahrain GP visitor surge at Sepang
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department (JIM) will ensure that immigration procedures involving visas and related passes at the country’s entry points run smoothly during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this October. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would work closely with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) to ensure clearance procedures at the country's entry points are carried out efficiently while complying with all security requirements. “We must provide the best possible service to ensure the smooth organisation of the Formula 1 event.

items.title: Immigration busts ‘flying passport’ syndicate, three arrested in Johor
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has dismantled a “flying passport” syndicate with the arrest of three suspects at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) in Gelang Patah, Johor, yesterday, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. He said the operation, which began at 10am, involved a team of officers and personnel from the Putrajaya Immigration headquarters Intelligence and Special Operations Division and Johor JIM. He said the team also seized mobile phones, keys to a premise, jewellery, Immigration security stamps and RM20,000 in cash.

items.title: Indonesian maid jailed four years for neglect that led to toddler’s drowning in Sentul pool
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — An Indonesian domestic helper was sentenced to four years’ jail by the Sessions Court here today after she pleaded guilty to neglecting a boy, resulting in his death by drowning in an adult swimming pool last month. According to the charge, Wahyuni, as a person responsible for the care of a two-year-three-month-old boy, neglected the child, resulting in his death. According to the facts of the case, the victim’s mother had instructed the accused, who was employed as her domestic helper, to take the victim and his five-year-old brother to the swimming pool at their residential complex on the day of the incident.

items.title: Remains of three policemen killed in Beaufort electrocution incident sent home after post-mortem
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The remains of three police officers who died believed to be from electrocution outside the Weston Police Station, Beaufort, yesterday afternoon were brought out from the Forensic Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE) at 2:55 pm today to be sent back to their respective hometowns. The remains of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong will be taken to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Air Operations Force (PGU) Airfield here before being flown to Sarawak. Meanwhile, Beaufort District Police Chief Supt Champin Piuh expressed his appreciation to Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun, members of the Sabah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK), and HQE for their extensive assistance in facilitating the management of the remains.

items.title: Bersatu sec‑gen Azmin Ali says party remains legitimate Perikatan component despite PAS claim
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali today hit back at PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s assertion that the party’s membership in Perikatan Nasional (PN) had automatically lapsed, describing the claim as unconstitutional. He stressed that Bersatu’s position could only be decided by the PN presidential council under Clause 7A of the coalition’s constitution. Therefore, Bersatu remains a legitimate component party of Perikatan Nasional,” Azmin said.

items.title: Border agency seizes falsely declared frozen chicken, pork worth RM3.42m at Sepanggar Port
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has seized 12 containers carrying frozen animal products worth an estimated RM3.42 million at Sepanggar Port. The seizure was the result of an enforcement operation targeting false import declarations. AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the seizure involved 348,000kg of frozen chicken and pork believed to have been brought into the country through declarations that did not match the cargo.

items.title: Anwar says GLICs deployed RM20.3b in domestic investments under GEAR-uP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — The Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP), which is entering its third year, saw government-linked investment companies (GLICs) allocating and deploying RM 20.3 billion domestically. “This (GEAR-uP) is not capital seeking passive returns. Much has been achieved, but much remains to be done,” Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in the GEAR-uP Progress Report released today.

items.title: Anwar says constituency funds belong to people, not exclusive right of elected MPs
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Aug 7 — Government funding allocated to a parliamentary constituency is intended for its constituents and is not the exclusive right of its elected Member of Parliament (MP), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the funds were meant to finance facilities and improvements that raised the living standards of the people in the constituency. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Melaka Police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar.

items.title: Government prioritises new theatres to support surgeries during Sultanah Aminah Hospital upgrades
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 7 — The Economy Ministry will prioritise building three to four new operating theatres at the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) while the mechanical and electrical (M&E) upgrades take place. Its minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the new operating theatres will complement the hospital’s existing 12 operating theatres that will also undergo part of the M&E upgrades. Akmal Nasrullah said the government will prioritise the building of the operating theatres to support ongoing surgeries and make way for the hospital’s upgrades.

items.title: AGC: Nicky Liow made RM10m payment to compound 26 money laundering charges
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — Businessman Liow Soon Hee, better known as Nicky Liow, paid RM10 million to settle money laundering charges after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) accepted his representation and withdrew 26 counts against him. Liow had faced 26 charges under Section 4 of the Anti Money Laundering, Anti Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613) at the Shah Alam Sessions Court on April 12, 2022. In line with Section 92 of Act 613, the AGC subsequently withdrew all charges against Liow.

items.title: Premises raided as IRB investigates individuals named in Tabung Haji RCI report, discrepancies found
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has opened investigations into individuals identified in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). In a statement, IRB said a tax risk analysis had found discrepancies between the individuals’ declared income and their asset holdings. “IRB officers had raided several related premises to gather information, examine documents and verify facts relevant to the investigations.

items.title: Four charged in Shah Alam court over false Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 applications
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 7 — Four individuals were charged in the Sessions Court here today over false statements in applications for incentives under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 career programme, dating back to two years ago. Foo Yon is accused of submitting a Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Confirmation Form on behalf of his company to a Perkeso agent at Taman Bukit Serdang, Seri Kembangan, on November 2, 2024. Four individuals were charged in the Sessions Court here today over false statements in applications for incentives under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 career programme, dating back to two years ago.

items.title: Perikatan and BN in negotiations for Melaka, Hadi says goal remains to ‘unite and save the Malays’
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang today confirmed that preliminary discussions have begun between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) on seat allocations for the upcoming Melaka state election. “The Melaka state assembly has not been dissolved, but discussions, particularly on Malay Muslim unity, are ongoing. He added that the negotiations would take into account the outcome of the last general election, when BN failed to secure any parliamentary seats in Melaka.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences to family of former CJ Mohamed Eusoff Chin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the entire family of former Chief Justice Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin, who died this morning. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said Mohamed Eusoff had rendered great service to the nation, particularly in strengthening the judicial institution throughout his career. Mohamed Eusoff, 91, was laid to rest at the Section 9 Muslim Cemetery in Kota Damansara.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh, KL mayor sample Kuching’s culinary scene
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud sampled a taste of Kuching’s culinary scene on Friday morning as part of their visit to the city. The two, who arrived in Kuching for a series of engagements, began the day with a visit to Kuching South Mayor Dato Wee Hong Seng. Wee later accompanied them to the Borneo Culinary World Cup (BCWC) 2026 at Chung Hua Primary School No.

items.title: Sarawak implements Education Ministry’s Child Protection Policy, parents among those required to sign compliance pledge
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Sarawak began implementing the Ministry of Education’s (MoE) Child Protection Policy (CPP) on July 27, months after the nationwide rollout was announced in January. Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the State Education Department has directed all district education offices to immediately implement the policy after receiving MoE Circulars (SPI) No. Under the CPP, individuals dealing with students and schools are required to sign a Student Protection Policy Compliance Pledge (Aku Janji), a core component of the policy.

items.title: N. Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim helms finance, security and investment portfolios
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim will lead three major portfolios in the state government administration for the 2026-2031 term, including Islamic Religious Affairs and Security; Finance, Land and Natural Resources; and Investment, Infrastructure, Utilities, Communications and Felda. The Juasseh state assemblyman also announced the appointment of ten State Government Councilors including retaining two Exco members, namely Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli (Linggi) and Mustapha Nagoor (Palong). Mohd Faizal was appointed as the Rural Development and Regional Development Exco, while Mustapha will retain his old portfolio as the Youth and Sports Development Exco.

items.title: Three men arrested after leading police on car chase in Sibu
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 7 — Three local men were arrested after allegedly leading police on a chase before being detained in Sungai Merah on Friday, with officers also seizing suspected housebreaking tools found inside their vehicle. Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the incident occurred at about 1.30am when a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) team conducting crime prevention patrols spotted a suspicious Toyota Vios at the Paradom roundabout. Abang Zainal said three local men were detained for further investigation, while police also seized the car and several items believed to be commonly used for housebreaking, including a bolt cutter and a metal pry tool.

items.title: Unsafe George Town heritage properties to be shuttered, MBPP vows strict enforcement on owners
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 7 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) is considering engaging qualified engineers to conduct visual inspections of heritage buildings within the George Town World Heritage Site. MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the city council is also considering introducing a requirement for heritage building owners to submit a structural assessment report to the council every two years. He said MBPP has identified 66 heritage buildings within the George Town World Heritage Site as being poorly maintained.

items.title: Serian joins Kuching, Samarahan as unhealthy API readings rise
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Serian recorded the highest unhealthy reading on the Air Pollutant Index (API) in Sarawak as of noon today, with a reading of 162. Three districts in Sarawak are now recording unhealthy API readings, consisting of Serian, Samarahan and Kuching. Other districts in Sarawak records moderate readings, ranging from 57 to 91.

items.title: Hadi says Bersatu no longer part of Perikatan after plans for new coalition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is no longer a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Abdul Hadi said the PN constitution provides that any party choosing to join or establish another alliance would automatically cease to be a member of the coalition. “They (Bersatu) have already stated their intention to want to form another ‘team’.
